slot.brief: Given the cell notation of a spontaneous cell at 298 K, ask which is the cathode / direction of electron flow / sign of ΔG — conceptual reasoning about E°cell without heavy computation.

stem: For the spontaneous cell Zn | Zn2+ (1.0 M) || Pb2+ (1.0 M) | Pb at 298 K (Given: E°(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V, E°(Pb2+/Pb) = -0.13 V), which statement is correct?
options: Pb electrode acts as the anode
Electrons flow from Pb to Zn in the external circuit

verdicts.working: E°cell = E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) − E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.13 − (−0.76) = +0.63 V. Thus ΔG = −nFE°cell < 0, so (C) is correct.

working:
Higher reduction potential electrode is cathode: Pb. Zn is anode. E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = -0.13 - (-0.76) = +0.63 V. Since E°cell > 0, ΔG = -nFE°cell < 0. Electrons flow externally from Zn to Pb.

Independent check: E°cell = E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) − E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.13 − (−0.76) = +0.63 V. Thus ΔG = −nFE°cell < 0, so (C) is correct.
solution:
The higher reduction potential electrode, Pb, is the cathode; Zn is the anode.
$$E^\fell = -0.13 - (-0.76) = +0.63\,\text{V}$$
Since $\Delta G = -nFE^\fell$, we have $\Delta G < 0$.
